reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
name: Glasgow Outcome Scale

version.label: GOS, five categories (Jennett & Bond 1975)
version.detail: 1 = death, 2 = vegetative state, 3 = severe disability, 4 = moderate disability, 5 = good recovery. Structured interview guidance (Wilson et al. 1998) is not reproduced.

purpose: Global functional outcome after brain injury.
intendedPopulation: Adults after traumatic or non-traumatic acute brain injury, usually after discharge.

calculatorNotice.title: Global outcome scale
calculatorNotice.message: Describes overall outcome, not neurological severity. A structured interview improves consistency.

inputDefinitions.label: Outcome category

options.label: Vegetative state
options.detail: Unresponsive and speechless; no evidence of meaningful responsiveness.

options.label: Severe disability
options.detail: Conscious but dependent on others for daily support.

options.label: Moderate disability
options.detail: Independent in daily life but disabled (e.g. unable to resume previous work or activities).

options.label: Good recovery
options.detail: Resumption of normal life, possibly with minor deficits.

inputDefinitions.help: Assign the category that best describes overall outcome.

resultStates.label: Good recovery
resultStates.summary: Outcome: good recovery at this assessment.
resultStates.detail: Minor deficits may persist; this describes global function, not every impairment.

clinicalContext.text: A widely used global outcome measure after brain injury.
Often dichotomised in studies (e.g. 4–5 versus 1–3); definitions vary.

clinicalInsights.text: Record the timepoint and the information source.
The extended GOS (GOSE) separates upper and lower bands within categories 3–5.

limitations.text: Broad categories are insensitive to smaller changes in outcome.

limitations: Inter-rater variability without a structured interview.
Reflects disability from all causes, not only the brain injury.

confounders.effect: Can lower the category independently of the brain injury.

guideSections.what: A five-category global outcome scale after brain injury.
guideSections.whenToUse: Follow-up outcome assessment after brain injury; research outcomes.
guideSections.howToPerform: Establish consciousness, independence in daily life, and return to previous activities, then assign the category that fits. A structured interview is recommended.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Used as an outcome measure, typically months after injury.

sources.citation: Jennett B, Bond M. Assessment of outcome after severe brain damage. Lancet. 1975;1(7905):480-484.
Wilson JTL, Pettigrew LEL, Teasdale GM. Structured interviews for the Glasgow Outcome Scale and the extended Glasgow Outcome Scale: guidelines for their use. J Neurotrauma. 1998;15(8):573-585.

licensing.note: The structured interview (© Wilson, Pettigrew, Teasdale 1998) is not reproduced.
